title: Position Papyrus as agent-accessible publishing on the marketing site
description: Ryan, 2026-10-20: agent accessibility is a core feature and part of Papyrus's positioning. On the Papyrus marketing site (p.apyr.us): a feature section/page explaining that every Papyrus site is readable by agents and people alike: per-page Markdown, llms.txt and llms-full.txt, Accept: text/markdown negotiation, page actions (Copy Markdown, open in AI assistants), RSS/Atom, sitemap and structured data; agents operating the newsroom through the CLI and API; roadmap: MCP and WebMCP. Include it in the homepage positioning and the features list (PPY-b9b038). Ship after PPY-f172d7 and the page-actions story are live, with real examples from a live site.

comments.author: home
comments.text: Live 2026-10-21: https://p.apyr.us/agent-accessible.html ('Readable by agents and people alike') plus an agents section on the home page and 'For agents' nav/footer links (Papyrus-web PRs #15, #20, #22; Amplify job 20 SUCCEED). Covers per-page Markdown twins, llms.txt and llms-full.txt, Accept: text/markdown negotiation (and exactly where it does not run: GitHub Pages docs sites, the two leaderboards), page actions Copy Markdown / View as Markdown / Open in ChatGPT, Claude, Perplexity (with the list of sites where the three links were curl-verified), RSS/Atom, sitemap, structured data, agents operating the newsroom through CLI and API, and MCP/WebMCP stated as NOT built. Real examples from live sites (pilobol.us index.md, llms.txt, llms-full.txt, feeds, an article with Accept negotiation) were each curled before citing. There is no separate features-list page on the site (PPY-b9b038 stays separate).
